subject: Order form: invoice routing, tax treatment & net terms
messages:
From: Amanda Lewis <amanda.lewis@fintrax.com>
To: rafael_mendes@redwood.com
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 13 Dec 2027 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Order Form — invoice entity, tax withholding & net terms questions

Hi Rafael,

Thanks for sending the redline of the Order Form earlier today. Procurement has a few quick operational questions we need clarified before we can route the PO and sign:

- Invoice recipient: can invoices be issued to Fintrax Holdings Ltd (our EU billing entity) rather than the US parent? If not, what evidence do you need to accept an EU remit entity?
- Net terms: your standard is Net 30 in the MSA, but finance is asking whether we can set Net 45 for this enterprise relationship. Is that acceptable?
- VAT/withholding: do you expect us to withhold any local taxes on payments, or will Redwood provide VAT invoicing (reverse-charge friendly) and confirm VAT registration details?
- PO / Attachment: we'll attach a PO once the remit path is confirmed. We also attached our tax certificate for review.

Can you loop in legal and ops so we have clear language in the Order Form about invoice recipient, the net terms for the first year, and any tax gross-up responsibilities? We want to avoid rework after signature.

Thanks,
Amanda Lewis
Head of Procurement — Fintrax
Fintrax Holdings Ltd
Attachments: Fintrax_tax_cert.pdf
From: rafael_mendes@redwood.com
To: Amanda Lewis <amanda.lewis@fintrax.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 13 Dec 2027 11:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Order Form — invoice entity, tax withholding & net terms questions

Amanda — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Kim (legal) and Lauren (finance ops) to confirm the recommended language and what evidence we need. Quick answers up front:

- Invoice entity: we can accept Fintrax Holdings Ltd as the invoice recipient provided we have a signed Order Form that references the invoice remit entity, and we collect a tax residency certificate (sounds like you've attached one). There may be additional evidence depending on jurisdiction (we'll call that out).
- Net terms: sales-side I'm neutral, but we tend to default to Net 30. If procurement needs Net 45 we can consider it for the first year tied to a 12-month commit; legal needs to approve the change to the Order Form.
- VAT/withholding: for EU customers we generally issue VAT invoices where applicable and accommodate reverse-charge language if Fintrax is VAT-registered. If withholding is required by local law, we need the tax treaty/residency docs and to reflect gross-up language in the payment clause.

Kim/Lauren — can you do two things: (1) propose a 1-paragraph Order Form insertion that ensures Redwood will invoice Fintrax Holdings Ltd (EU remit) with the required tax fields, and (2) confirm whether we can accept Net 45 on a deal-level basis (deal id RDW-2027-FTX-982) with a 12-month minimum commit condition? I'm attaching our current redline of the Order Form (OrderForm_Redwood_v3_redlines.docx) for context.

Rafael Mendes
Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
Attachments: OrderForm_Redwood_v3_redlines.docx
From: kimberly_park@redwood.com
To: rafael_mendes@redwood.com, Amanda Lewis <amanda.lewis@fintrax.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 14 Dec 2027 08:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Order Form — invoice entity, tax withholding & net terms questions

Amanda / team — quick legal note and proposed redline. Apologies for the long email but I wanted to be explicit to avoid back-and-forth after signature.

Proposed insertion for Order Form (short paragraph to sit under "Billing and Payment"):
"Billing Entity: Customer acknowledges that Redwood will issue invoices to the billing entity specified in the Order Form (Fintrax Holdings Ltd). Customer shall provide reasonable documentation of the billing entity, including, where applicable, a tax residency certificate or VAT registration number. Redwood will use the remit-to entity and tax information provided on the Order Form for invoicing and tax reporting purposes. Where local law requires withholding, the Order Form will state whether payments shall be grossed up for withholding taxes or whether Customer will withhold and provide proof of payment to the relevant authority."

Net terms: we can approve Net 45 for the first 12 months if the customer signs a 12-month minimum commit and agrees to an accelerated payment remedy (service suspension for delinquent accounts after 60 days). I'll add that as a line in the Order Form.

VAT/withholding: for EU reverse-charge we will include the VAT number on the invoice and the reverse-charge note. If Fintrax is withholding under domestic law, we need the treaty/residency docs. Also request that the customer confirm the local tax point of contact for remittance reconciliation.

I'll attach a one-page summary we can paste into the final Order Form. If that language is acceptable Amanda, we'll incorporate it into the redline and send for signature + the PO.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel — Redwood Inference
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: Amanda Lewis <amanda.lewis@fintrax.com>, rafael_mendes@redwood.com
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 15 Dec 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Order Form — invoice entity, tax withholding & net terms questions

Amanda — appreciate the quick turn. From sales/ops perspective:

- Net 45 with a 12-month minimum commit works for us; it keeps the economics intact if Fintrax commits to the usage band we discussed.
- We'll accept the EU remit entity. Please confirm the exact legal name and VAT/Tax ID to match on the Order Form.
- Once Kimberly's language is in, I will push the redline to DocuSign and notify finance operations to expect the PO and process the entity mapping.

Can you confirm by EOD (Thu) if Fintrax will accept the Net 45 + 12-month minimum? If yes, I'll proceed to DocuSign and attach the PO when available.

Thanks — Karthik
Senior Account Executive — Redwood Inference
